basis: Defining renal hypoplasia/aplasia and middle-ear malformations with hearing loss; genital anomalies have no axis.
Malignancy arising in the nasal cavity, which belongs to the airway axis.
Defining brain malformations, severe myopia and deafness; renal tubulopathy/proteinuria ~100%. Diaphragmatic defects (~50-70%) omitted by cap.
Endocervicitis is usually infectious; the reproductive site itself has no organ axis.
Peroxisomal disorder with defining growth/muscle abnormalities and pericardial constriction (31/42); hepatic disease with hepatomegaly in 37/42. Minor ocular findings excluded.
Total albinism and congenital deafness define the syndrome; frequencies of intellectual disability and hypogonadism are unspecified.
Benign neoplasm confined to the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Squamous cell carcinoma arising in skin.
Inherited retinal cone degeneration with impaired visual acuity and color vision.
Inborn amino-acid transport defect with impaired renal reabsorption and aminoaciduria. Intellectual disability is occasional; kidney stones are separately diagnosed.
Defined by impaired development of intellectual, motor or social functions; neurodevelopmental disorders belong to the neurologic axis.
Autoimmune coagulation disorder defined by antiphospholipid antibodies and vascular thrombosis; ocular damage is not established as common.
Vitreous adhesion directly distorts and damages the macula.
Mature T-cell lymphoma; no individual extranodal organ is consistently affected in most patients across the umbrella.
Usually an ascending infection of the female reproductive tract; reproductive organs have no axis. Perihepatitis is a minority complication.
Defining tubulopathy, diabetes and cerebellar degeneration; blindness/retinopathy in 1/1 assessed. Bone/muscle disease, deafness and skin changes omitted by cap.
Defining hair/skin/nail disease and oral cleft/dental anomalies; intellectual disability and hypogonadism each frequent (30-79%). Syndactyly is cutaneous.
Progressive encephalopathy and neuromotor degeneration; muscle wasting/weakness in nearly all assessed and osteoporosis in 9/12 support musculoskeletal involvement.
Disease of intracranial arterial walls. Subarachnoid hemorrhage (7/17) is a separately diagnosed rupture complication.
Localized cutaneous mucin deposition with papules, nodules and fibrosis; absence of thyroid disease excludes an endocrine label.
Distal arthrogryposis and ectodermal dysplasia establish joint and skin/appendage involvement; no evidence supports additional axes.
Recurrent bacterial infection of hair follicles and surrounding skin, usually caused by Staphylococcus aureus.
Intermittent strabismus is a disorder of ocular alignment and motility.
Defined by skeletal malformations including wormian skull bones and brachydactyly; cardiac disease of the distinct gain-of-function syndrome is not inferred.
Gestational trophoblastic malignancy arising in the ovary; reproductive origin has no axis, and metastatic sites are not established as common.
